comment: Sandeater, front man for The Desert Demons, invites you to play at their Desert Aid-gala.\n\tAll revenue goes to the thirsty desert-peoples of  the world. Theres no pay, but maybe some good publicity.\n\tAnd of course to help the thirsty people.

Desert Aid is a success.\n\tExcept that the Palladium is sold out, City News prints a full page on <¤Cband.Name> and Desert Demons, reporting on your strong dedication to the cause of the thirsty desert-peoples of the world.

Desert Aid wasn't such a great idea after all.\n\tJust a few school groups on an excursion showed up for the concert. City News prints a paragraph declaring both <¤cband.name> and Desert Demons idiots. Nobody lives in the desert, so there's no one who needs help!\n\tNo great day for <¤cband.name>.

Superstars Ghost in the Machine offer <¤cband.name> to open for their upcoming tour.\n\tThey will do eight shows around the world and it would be an opportunity for <¤cband.name> to play abroad.\n\tGhost in the Machine wants you to pay $50.000 to support them.

You still haven't signed a contract with Rainbow records, and Global honcho G. Jerome Vonderbaldt is getting edgy.\n\tThe only way for his plan to work is through a record deal with Rainbow, so get to it!

There could be no doubt about your task: Your mission was to sign with Rainbow Records and bury them.\n\tGlobal even reminded you about the details, and you still haven't taken the first step towards finishing the plan!\n\tYou're all out of chances, manager.

Oh, come on! You're going bring Rainbow down by signing with a different label?\n\tThat would be a clever idea if that was what Global had asked you to do. When you work with Global, you should follow their instructions.\n\tYou won't be working with them anymore.

For Global's plan to proceed, you need to have a record contract with Rainbow.\n\tHowever, you just cancelled you're contract with Rainbow, terminating Global's plan!\n\tIt should come as no surprise when Global fires your moronic ass!
Rainbow Records boss Karen McLaren is devastated that you can't keep the members of  <¤Cband.name> together.\n\tThat band is her golden calf, you know. All of Rainbow's future is invested in them.
That's the second band member quitting <¤Cband.name>. Rainbow doesn't trust you as a manager anymore.\n\tSorry, but you're out.

Rainbow boss Karen McLaren is disappointed that <¤cband.name>'s career isn't moving as fast as they had hoped.\n\tShe reluctantly approves an additional $40.000 advance to give them a push in the right direction.
Rainbow is really mad at you for spending all of its money on useless ad campaigns.\n\tYou're fired.

Rainbow is angry with you for spending all their money on strange and probably illegal services from known criminals.\n\tYou cannot convince the label that such action is necessary, because Rainbow Records is not going to run an illegal operation.\n
Rainbow is angry with you for spending all of its money on gifts to the band.\n\tRainbow Records is not in the habit of spoiling of its artists and that policy applies to you, too.\n

Rainbow Records boss Karen McLaren is concerned that <¤Cband.name> still hasn't become the new hit artist her label badly needs.\n\tHowever, at a board meeting Rainbow has decided to put the last of its financial resources into this project, sink or swim.\n\tAll the label has is $40.000, so put it to good use.

Trying to hold back tears of anger, Rainbow boss Karen McLaren explains that your total incompetence as a manager has ruined the company.\n\tRainbow Records had a forty year history as a record label, often releasing artists that the bigger labels wouldn't sign, and thereby making invaluable contributions to the music industry.\n\tRainbow used to be the music lover's label, but that's all over now because of you.
Rainbow is angry with you for spending so much money on useless ad campaigns.\n\tKaren McLaren doubts whether you are the right person for the job.

Rainbow is angry with you for spending so much money on strange and probably illegal services from known criminals.\n\tThe company does not believe such action is necessary, simply because Rainbow will not operate illegally.
Rainbow is very angry with you for spending so much of its money on gifts to the band.\n\tRainbow Records is not in the habit of spoiling its artists, and that policy applies to you, too.

<missionVar.YouSuckMusician.name> thinks you are a useless manager.\n\tWhy won't you even try just a little bit? Don't you want to make it?\n\tDon't you know that Rainbow's future depends on your success?

<missionVar.YouSuckMusician.name> is on to you!\n\t{X;Pron;S3;[#Gender:<¤CRealMusician.gender>]} knows about your deal with Global Records and the plan to run Rainbow out of business.\n\t{X;Pron;S3;[#Gender:<¤CRealMusician.gender>]} threatens to expose the entire plan to Rainbow unless {x;Pron;S3;[#Gender:<¤CRealMusician.gender>]} gets part of the action: a new $5000 wide screen television!

Rainbow Records discovered that you are a traitor.\n\tThe company fired you out of anger, and has hired thugs to beat you to a pulp. You will never set foot in Rock City again.\n\tGlobal denies any knowledge of your existence.
The plan was to bring Rainbow down by not selling any records, but now it seems that <¤Cband.name> are making sales.\n\tGlobal Records worries that you won't deliver.

Global Records fires you.\n\tYou've sold too many records and <¤Cband.name> are becoming an important asset for Rainbow Records.\n\tQuite the opposite of the original plan! It seems that Rainbow might even make it, a delight to the world's true music lovers but much to the grief of your employer.

Rainbow boss Karen McLaren is furious that you have spent all of the label's money without releasing a record.\n\tThis is not what she had in mind, and you better believe that Rainbow won't throw cash around like some other labels.\n\tYou're fired.

Global honcho G. Jerome Vonderbaldt suggests that you waste all of Rainbow's money on useless stuff to help cause the small label's failure.\n\tHe suggests you also squeeze as much cash as possible out of the flower-lovers.\n\tHowever, it's imperative that Rainbow doesn't know about the plan. Be careful!
What have you learned about money? Don't waste it!\n\tConsider that when you start over.

You were supposed to bring Rainbow down by spending all their money. In that case, you better try to sell as few records as possible. Otherwise, you're making them money, do you see? Don't sell so many records next time, okay?

You're supposed to sign with Rainbow. The plan was to bring them down by spending all their money. For that to work you need a record contract with Rainbow, right? Try again and try not to be so stupid this time around, OK?

You're supposed to sign with Rainbow. The plan was to bring them down by spending all their money. For that to work you need a record contract with Rainbow, right? Try again and try not to be so stupid this time around, OK?
Now, for the plan to work out, you have to stick with Rainbow. Keep the contract with them at any cost. Make sure they have no reason to fire you!

Rainbow-boss Karen McLaren is furious that you have spent all her label's money on song licenses.\n\tThe Rainbow funds are limited! You're an experienced manager and should make do with one or two songs.\n\tFeeling deceived by your incompetence, Karen McLaren terminates your agreement.
Rainbow boss Karen McLaren thinks you are unfit to manage her artists.\n\tHow can you record so many songs and not sell any of them?

A handful of fans have set up camp outside the practice room. They sleep in tents and cook on camp stoves.\n\tEvery time somebody comes or goes, the fans take pictures and ask for autographs.\n\tAt first the band enjoys the attention, but quickly get tired.
